ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory protocol: (1) identify and verify each director, incorporator, and all UBOs holding 25% or more; (2) determine domestic and foreign PEP status, including family members and known close associates; (3) screen against Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the UK sanctions list, and the OFAC SDN List, given that Stripe and PayPal clear USD payments through U.S. financial institutions; (4) document source of funds for initial capitalization; (5) prepare a written low-risk AML/CFT assessment consistent with FINTRAC guidance for e-commerce merchant accounts; (6) re-screen all parties immediately prior to filing Articles of Incorporation and again at bank and payment processor onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (official online portal administered by the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery) at https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry; NUANS name search report prepared by an approved service provider.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under the Ontario Business Corporations Act must be expressed in English or French, or both on a bilingual basis. Latin-script transliteration is required for non-Roman characters, and the NUANS search is performed on the Latin-alphabet rendering. A name generally comprises a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'); numerals and initials are permitted. The name must not be confusingly similar to any existing Ontario corporate name, registered trademark, or trade name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying Crown or government sponsorship: 'Royal', 'Crown', 'Municipal', 'Government', 'Minister', 'Approved'
Words requiring prior ministerial or regulator consent, including 'Ontario', 'Canada', and 'Canadian', which are permissible only with contextual justification or written approval
Obscene, scandalous, or deceptive terms, and any names implying a connection with a government body, the Crown, or an existing trademark
Any term that renders the proposed name confusingly similar to an existing corporate name or registered mark under OBCA s. 9
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS report is valid for 90 days; if incorporation is not completed within that window, a new search and report must be purchased. Upon name rejection, the applicant may: (1) submit a written reconsideration request to the Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, setting out the distinctiveness of the proposed name and the steps already taken to distinguish it from conflicting marks; (2) file a written consent from the holder of the conflicting corporate name or trademark; (3) if the Ministry upholds the rejection, select a new distinctive name and obtain a fresh NUANS report, or appeal to the Director under OBCA s. 10(2) and the applicable regulations. For a federal CBCA incorporation, the equivalent appeal is a written submission to the Director of Corporations Canada, who may issue an adjudicated reconsideration decision under the CBCA Regulations, s. 12.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical Ontario street address is mandatory for the registered office under OBCA s. 12; a post office box is prohibited. A 'virtual office' or registered-agent commercial address is generally accepted for an online auto-parts e-commerce corporation, provided the location is a real, staffed premises capable of receiving service of process, statutory notices, and written records. As the business is digital-only, no commercial storefront is required, and ISIC 4791 does not require a statutory license, so no additional physical premises or Ontario asset nexus is required beyond the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, with an estimated 3-5% annual probability of any unannounced physical inspection. Ontario Business Registry compliance is primarily documentary; physical visits occur only upon complaints, fraud flags, or service-of-process failures. The Canada Revenue Agency conducts records-based audits without physical visits in more than 90% of small and medium enterprise cases, and GST/HST registration and payroll source deduction verification are performed by mail or digital correspondence. The low-risk e-commerce profile under standard FINTRAC banking risk tiering does not ordinarily attract field inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, ss. 4, 5, 8, 15, 17, 115 and 125; Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39, s. 3 (Initial Return); O. Reg. 289/00 (Forms) under the OBCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Director, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CIPPSB), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery of Ontario, operating through the Ontario Business Registry (online filing portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under O. Reg. 289/00 under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario)).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the OBCA; share capital and classes are specified in the Articles. No escrow account is mandated for subscription proceeds; funds may be deposited into a Canadian-domiciled corporate bank account. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the voting shares unless sectoral filing thresholds apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry — Name Search Module (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada NUANS system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a distinct corporate name is used, conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report for Ontario and federal conflicts. The name must not be confusing with an existing Ontario or federal corporation or registered trade-mark. If a numbered designation such as Ontario Business Number Inc. is preferred, this step is skipped. Submit the proposed name electronically and rely on the registry-issued NUANS report attached to the Articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (legible, in Roman letters)
NUANS search report (dated within 90 days prior to filing)
Incorporator's name, address, and signature block
Declaration of non-confusion where required by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried under s. 9 OBCA for confusion, file an amended Articles submission with a corrected distinct name, or request a numbered company designation (Ontario Business Number Inc.) by re-filing through the Ontario Business Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (Director, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch) — online incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) electronically: set out the corporation name or numbered designation, registered office address in Ontario, minimum and maximum number of directors (or exact number), share classes and rights, restrictions on share transfers or business activities (if any), and any additional provisions permitted under s. 5 OBCA. E-file and pay the statutory filing fee; upon approval the registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation with an Ontario corporation file number.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation
NUANS name search report (if a named corporation is used)
Certified identity of incorporator and director consents
Ontario Business Registry authenticated account credentials
Payment via credit card or Ontario Business Registry deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice or rejects the Articles, cure within the stated period by re-filing corrected Articles online; if rejection is based on unlawful objects or improper share provisions, revise the Articles to comply with OBCA ss. 4–5 and re-file without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Return Filing and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry — CIPPSB (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of the date of incorporation, file the Initial Return electronically. Confirm the registered office is a physical address in Ontario (not a post-office box), identify the first directors, and record the Registered Office Information Record holder. The corporation must maintain the registered office records and the registry information must be kept current under the Corporations Information Act.
required_dossiers: Initial Return (electronic form via Ontario Business Registry)
Certificate of Incorporation and file number
Registered office lease, sublease, or landlord's written consent
List of first directors with residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is not filed within 60 days, the corporation is placed in default and risks administrative dissolution under the Corporations Information Act; cure by immediate electronic filing and, if the corporation has been dissolved, apply for revival under OBCA s. 241 with payment of arrears and late fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Ontario corporation for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts: Corporation Income Tax (RC account), GST/HST (RT account, mandatory when worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), and Payroll (RP account) only when employees are engaged. File the corporate information return and confirm the fiscal year-end date selected in the Articles. Non-resident directors are permitted, but the corporation must provide any required information circular on resident directors where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Ontario file number
Directors' full names, dates of birth, and residential addresses
Fiscal year-end date (e.g., December 31)
RC1 — Request for a Business Number form (electronic)
Corporate bank account details for GST/HST refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the registration for identity verification, resubmit the RC1 with certified true copies of the Certificate of Incorporation and government-issued identification for each director; if the GST/HST account is blocked, request a clearance letter from the Ontario Business Registry confirming the corporate status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Organization: Minute Book, By-laws, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private sector — registered law firm or licensed paralegal corporate governance counsel (no governmental SLA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate minute book containing the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, By-law No. 1 (general business conduct, meetings, indemnification), the First Board Resolution, organizational minutes, share certificates in respect of issued common shares, the share register, transfer ledger, and the Registered Office Information Record. Execute all documents with the corporate seal where required by the by-laws.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolutions (by-law adoption, officer appointment, share issuance)
Share subscription agreements and closing bank records
Registry of directors and officers
Registered Office Information Record holder's written consent
Unanimous shareholders' agreement, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minute book is defective due to missing quorum, lost signature pages, or incomplete share issuance, convene a curative directors' meeting or obtain a sole shareholder's written resolution to ratify all prior actions pursuant to OBCA ss. 115 and 116.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial Occupancy, Zoning and Fire Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Building and Fire Prevention Departments (municipality-specific, e.g., City of Toronto Municipal Licensing and Standards, Building Division, and Fire Prevention Division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a commercial occupancy permit from the local municipal building department confirming compliance with the applicable Zoning By-law and the Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 332/12). Schedule a fire safety inspection under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07) for the warehousing and dispatch areas, verifying aisle widths, sprinkler systems, charging bays for powered equipment, and storage limits for combustible goods. Where the employer hires workers, register with the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB).
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and landlord's occupancy consent
Site plan and floor plan showing storage layout and emergency exits
Fire safety inspection request and occupancy load calculation
Municipal business licence application, wherever applicable
WSIB registration confirmation (if work is performed by employees)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire or building inspection results identify deficiencies, comply with the correction order and schedule a re-inspection; municipal licence denials may be appealed within 30 days through the local Administrative Tribunal or Municipal Licensing and Standards Committee and, in Ontario municipalities, further to the Ontario Building Code Act appeal process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (municipal implementation); municipal building and fire departments (e.g., City of Toronto Building Division and Fire Prevention Division); Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP) for environmental registrations and waste management permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Occupancy Permit (Ontario Building Code, O. Reg. 332/12) and municipal business licence where applicable. No sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is prescribed for ISIC 4791 / NAICS 441310 online auto parts retail; the Motor Vehicle Dealers Act, 2002, S.O. 2002, c. 30, s. 1(1) does not apply to a retail seller of aftermarket parts and accessories only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP) — Environmental Assessment and Permissions Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-only category under the Environmental Assessment Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.18; a full Environmental Impact Statement is not triggered for warehousing, distribution, and online resale of automotive parts lacking on-site vehicle dismantling or hazardous waste processing. Where waste oil, lead-acid batteries, or coolants are accumulated, the operator must register as a Hazardous Waste Generator under O. Reg. 347 (General — Waste Management).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharges to municipal sewers must comply with local sewer-use by-laws and the Ontario Water Resources Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.40; no process wastewater is expected for e-commerce picking and packing. Air emissions: volatile organic compound releases from stored solvents, aerosols, and sealants must stay within the Local Air Quality criteria of O. Reg. 419/05 (Air Pollution — Local Air Quality). Waste: used oils, filters, brake fluids, and batteries must be stored in permitted containers, manifested, and transported to certified receivers under O. Reg. 347; spill prevention and reporting obligations under the Environmental Protection Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.19 apply to any release above prescribed thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07) fire safety certification covering extinguishers, smoke alarms, exit signage, and storage aisle clearances; structural load inspection of mezzanine and pallet racking under the Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 332/12); WSIB (Workplace Safety and Insurance Board) clearance certificate when the business employs workers; Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD) compliance inspection under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1 for materials handling equipment, ergonomic injury prevention, and warehouse safety programs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada - GST/HST Division and Business Number Registration; primary portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account, and GST/HST NETFILE. Ontario corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement with the Ontario Ministry of Finance; the Ontario Ministry of Finance separately operates the Ontario Tax Accounts portal for the Employer Health Tax (EHT) and the Ontario Business Registry for provincial corporate-registry data. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) is the customs authority for import/export accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Determine registration duty: a Canadian-incorporated business corporation must apply to the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RM (customs import/export), and RP (payroll, where employees are engaged). Step 2 - Foreign-owned entities: registration is made online through Business Registration Online (BRO) where the filer holds a CRA My Business Account credential; alternatively, submit a completed Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) to the Sudbury Tax Centre, attaching certified copies of the articles of incorporation (under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Ontario Business Corporations Act), the foreign-parent registration certificate (if applicable), and the Ontario corporate information schedules administered within the T2 corporate income tax return. Step 3 - Program-account activation: the CRA issues the BN and RT account (VAT ID format, e.g., 123456789RT0001); the GST/HST registration becomes effective on the earlier of the date the first taxable supply was made in Canada or the date of the application, with retroactive registration available under subsection 242(1) of the Excise Tax Act. An application must be filed within 30 days of ceasing to be a small supplier. Step 4 - Ontario specifics: no separate Ontario GST/HST account exists because the 8% provincial HST component is collected and remitted by the CRA; the corporation must, however, register with the Ontario Ministry of Finance for Employer Health Tax if Ontario payroll remuneration exceeds the CAD 1,000,000 annual exemption, and with the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) where workers are physically located in Ontario. Step 5 - Customs: an RM (import/export) program account under the same BN must be activated for the CBSA process to clear imported inventory (e.g., auto parts sourced abroad) and to file eManifest and export declarations. Step 6 - Non-resident shareholders do not require a separate Canadian tax TIN for the domestic corporation; the entity itself is the taxpayer, and non-resident shareholders/directors may require an individual CRA tax number only if they file a Canadian personal or withholding return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - CA_CORP is a Canadian-resident corporation (deemed resident under ITA subsection 250(4) by virtue of incorporation in Canada) and is taxed at the entity level on worldwide income under Part I of the Income Tax Act; no pass-through treatment is available to shareholders. Federal corporate income tax applies at the general rate of 15%, reduced to 9% on active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) up to the CAD 500,000 federal business limit; Ontario corporate income tax applies at 11.5% general rate, 3.2% for CCPC small-business income, and 10% for manufacturing and processing income. Where the corporation is controlled by non-residents it is not a CCPC, and the general federal and Ontario rates apply in full. The GST/HST is a separate value-added tax collected from customers and remitted to the CRA and does not alter the entity-level income tax classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; corporate status is statutory and may be displaced only through formal reorganization. Elections available to CA_CORP include: (i) voluntary registration for GST/HST while still a small supplier (ETA subsection 240(1)); (ii) election to use simplified net-tax accounting or annual GST/HST remittance frequency where the registrant qualifies as a small remitter under ETA section 237.1 and the related regulations; (iii) election under ITA subsection 85(1) for a tax-deferred rollover of property into the corporation on capital reorganization; (iv) election under ITA subsection 89(11) to treat the corporation as not being a CCPC where foreign-control facts are present; (v) the branch-tax election under ITA section 219 is limited to non-resident corporations and is not available to a domestic operating corporation; (vi) hybrid-mismatch rules under ITA sections 18.4, 18.5, and 18.6 are mandatory and contain no taxpayer election, while treaty-based fiscal-transparency elections (e.g., Canadian administrative recognition of a US LLC's check-the-box classification) affect only cross-border investors and do not alter the Canadian corporation's own classification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) - central monetary authority and supervisor of the retail payments framework - together with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI, prudential supervisor of deposit-taking institutions) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC, AML/ATF authority). Foreign exchange administration is liberalised under the Currency Act and the federal Bank Act; no exchange-control or central-bank licensing regime exists for FX operations because the wartime foreign-exchange control regime was dismantled in 1951. The Department of Finance Canada retains jurisdiction over sanctions and the Investment Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current-account (trade in goods and services, royalties, interest, dividends) and capital-account (share capital injections, shareholder loans, M&A, profit repatriation) transactions. There are no conversion ceilings, no prior approvals from the BOC or Department of Finance, and no non-resident ownership restrictions affecting an online retail treasury. Profit remittance is unrestricted: a Canadian corporation may declare and pay dividends in CAD or foreign currency without any profit remittance permit, but Part XIII withholding (statutory 25%; treaty-reduced, e.g., 5%-15% under the Canada-US treaty and 15% under the Canada-China treaty) is applied by the resident payer and remitted to the Canada Revenue Agency; this is a tax mechanics step, not an FX control. Practical impediments are limited to (i) FINTRAC reporting thresholds (C$10,000 for EFT and cross-border currency movements), (ii) AML source-of-funds checks when banks open treasury accounts, and (iii) the Investment Canada Act, which requires a non-Canadian establishing a new Canadian business to file a Notification with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada; a net-benefit review is triggered only for high-value acquisitions of control (2024 WTO-investor threshold: C$2.477 billion). None of these restraints affects current-account or ordinary treasury conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not require exporters to surrender, convert, or repatriate export proceeds within any statutory timeline. Export invoices may be denominated in CAD, USD, EUR, CNY or any freely convertible currency, and settlement can be collected in foreign accounts or converted at the corporate treasury's discretion. Administrative reporting that may touch export proceeds: (i) CBSA B13A export declaration for goods leaving Canada with a value above C$2,000 per shipment (electric courier and postal programs apply for low-value online retail parcels); (ii) GST/HST zero-rating of exported goods (the Ontario HST of 13% does not apply to qualifying exports; input tax credits remain available); (iii) FINTRAC EFT reporting by the receiving bank for cross-border transfers of C$10,000 or more; (iv) CRA reporting of foreign-source income and foreign-exchange gains; and (v) the base-erosion and anti-avoidance rules in the Income Tax Act if capital arrangements are structured to strip Canadian profits. None of these constitutes a surrender, conversion, or repatriation mandate.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the corporation has more than 50 shareholders or is a reporting issuer or a subsidiary of a reporting issuer
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under Canadian GAAP

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required for private corporations; beneficial ownership details updated upon shareholding transfers or director changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A combined Ontario general corporate income tax rate of 25% (15% federal + 10% provincial). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may claim the small business deduction, reducing the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, and Ontario small business deduction further reduces the provincial rate to 3.2%, resulting in an effective combined rate of 12.2% on eligible active business income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal corporate income tax return: Form T2 (Corporation Income Tax Return) filed electronically via CRA's E-filing, Internet File Transfer, or approved tax preparation software. Ontario corporate tax is integrated into the T2 return and filed with the Ontario Ministry of Finance through the T2 e-file system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Quarterly instalments are generally required for corporations with tax payable greater than CAD 3,000, due on the last day of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, and fiscal year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm Canadian business number (BN); non-resident corporations must include the BN assigned by CRA and indicate permanent establishment provinces.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) before taxes from financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source business income and any income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment; adjust for foreign exchange and treaty sourcing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after non-capital loss, capital loss, and other deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute only Canadian-source taxable income; non-residents claim deductions only against Canadian-source income as permitted under the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable before credits (Federal base tax calculation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applicable to all corporations with Canadian taxable income including non-resident corporations with a PE in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable capital gains and allowable capital losses from dispositions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gains from taxable Canadian property dispositions; treaty relief may reduce but not exempt unless treaty application filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate small business deduction eligibility and business limit allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations are excluded from CCPC status; this schedule generally not applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax computation for Ontario permanent establishments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only if the non-resident has a permanent establishment in Ontario; allocate gross revenue and salaries/wages to Ontario.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months, minimum CAD 100. Repeated failure adds another 5% plus 1% monthly. Interest charges at prescribed rates apply to unpaid tax and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced Canadian dividend withholding tax under an income tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Residency (form NR301 for waiver or NR302 for refund) from the foreign tax authority and submit it to the Canadian payor or CRA. The treaty rate must be certified under the Canada-US treaty (typically 5% for 10%+ corporate shareholders, 15% for portfolio investors).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%; treaty rates often reduced to 10% for industrial royalties (e.g., Canada-US, Canada-UK) or 0% for cultural or software copyright royalties where treaty applicable. Interest: statutory 25%; treaty rate commonly 10% (e.g., Canada-US), or 10% under Canada-UK.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million gross revenue threshold for Local File and CAD 10 million for Master File based on specified transaction sizes under IC 87-2R.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable to cross-border related-party transactions under ITA 247 and OECD guidelines. Canada does not apply Caribbean-style ESR (Economic Substance Regulations), but requires substantive activities and real economic presence for treaty shopping defenses and GAAR avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully evading Canadian income tax by understating e-commerce revenues, hiding online sales through undisclosed Stripe/PayPal accounts, or failing to report taxable Canadian income attributable to an Ontario permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under ITA section 239: fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; CRA civil penalties: gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax; compound daily interest; forfeiture orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding and source deductions; courts can issue warrants for arrest, travel bans, and restitution orders; director disqualification and personal liability for civil fraud where they knowingly participate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a shell entity in a low-tax jurisdiction with no real economic substance to book e-commerce procurement and strip profits from the Canadian operating company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment denying tax benefits; transfer pricing adjustment plus 10% penalty; fines and potential criminal liability if facts are misrepresented to CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns are exposed to civil personal liability and gross negligence penalties; professional disqualification, travel restrictions, and asset seizures for fraud under Canadian criminal code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using shell bank accounts and anonymous payment processing to launder proceeds from unreported online sales, structuring deposits to avoid FINTRAC reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Money Laundering under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: fines up to CAD 500,000 for individuals / CAD 2,000,000 for corporations, imprisonment up to 10 years; FINTRAC administrative penalties and bank freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as 'persons acting in a management capacity' may face criminal liability; personal asset freezing, travel bans, extradition exposure; director veils pierced for wilful blindness and failure to maintain AML internal controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Foreign Assets and Non-Resident Withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of dividends to non-resident shareholders without withholding 25% Canadian withholding tax; failing to file Part XIII returns; failing to report Canadian accounts or foreign income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax assessments at 25% plus interest and penalties; false omission penalties under ITA 162-163; criminal liability for failing to withhold under ITA 227.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unremitted withholding tax under ITA 227.1; directors' personal bank accounts can be garnished; travel bans and civil liability for breach of fiduciary duty to the corporation and foreign shareholders.
